app.name: ThoughtSpot MongoDB Atlas + Voyage Retrieval POV
out_of_scope: Raw binary file upload/download: The authoritative data model explicitly keeps raw binaries out of MongoDB and stores only source_uri/extracted text; no query pattern supports blob retrieval.

Automatic reranking execution endpoint: Rerank scores are represented in query_results results payloads, but no authoritative query pattern defines a standalone rerank operation. Reranking may occur inside retrieval services before persisting results, but not as a separate contract endpoint.

Delete endpoints for documents, benchmark runs, queries, or results: Possible via CRUD in principle, but not required by the authoritative query patterns or POV scope; omitted to avoid inventing unneeded lifecycle APIs.
Agent conversation/session database APIs: The authoritative model explicitly excludes a separate session/conversation collection.
notes: Principle: Endpoints are limited to straightforward CRUD on the authoritative data model or direct wrappers around the authoritative query patterns.

Principle: No API is introduced for unsupported capabilities such as raw binary file storage, authentication/authorization subsystem management, or agent session database management beyond the modeled entities.
Principle: Tenant scope is explicit in nearly all endpoints because the data model and query patterns are tenant-scoped.
Conventions: base_path=/api/v1; content_type=application/json; tenant_identifier=tenantId path parameter carrying tenants._id; timestamps=ISO-8601 strings; object_id=24-char hex string

collections.name: tenants
collections.description: Tenant/customer isolation boundary for uploaded documents, agent memory, benchmark runs, and queries. Included because Tenant is an explicit business entity and retrieval/evaluation flows are tenant-scoped.

collections.name: documents
collections.description: Top-level customer-provided content and conversation-derived memory documents used for retrieval. Stores source metadata and extracted text, while raw binary may remain external (e.g. S3) per current-state integration context.

structured_attributes.description: Flexible structured metadata used for hybrid retrieval filters, e.g. product area, connector source, labels, timestamps.

access.description: Optional access association carried at document level; included as current-state-aligned metadata, not as a separate entitlement system.

collections.name: chunk_profiles
collections.description: Definition of chunking strategies used in the POV/demo and benchmarking harness. Separated so the same document can be chunked multiple ways without duplicating strategy metadata on every chunk.

parameters.description: Strategy-specific settings such as chunk_size, overlap, separators, semantic thresholds.

collections.name: chunks
collections.description: Retrieval unit derived from documents. Stores chunk text, chunking strategy used, embedding vector, and ranking metadata needed for semantic retrieval and reranking experiments.

structured_attributes.description: Metadata copied/derived from document for hybrid filtering at chunk retrieval time.

rerank_text.description: Optional text optimized for reranker input, if different from chunk text.

collections.name: queries
collections.description: User questions and benchmark prompts submitted against a tenant corpus. Captures both ad hoc demo questions and benchmark questions with optional ground truth linkage.

document_scope.description: Optional constraints for on-the-fly demo queries or benchmark subsets.

collections.name: benchmark_runs
collections.description: A side-by-side POV evaluation execution context for a corpus, retrieval configuration, and comparison target(s). Captures the benchmark session the customer requested, including top-k metrics and latency measurements across approaches.

comparison_targets.description: Systems being compared in the run.

collections.name: query_results
collections.description: Stores retrieval outputs and evaluation metrics per query per compared approach. This collection is the measurement backbone for precision/recall/top-k/latency comparisons requested in the POV.

results.description: Ordered retrieval set for the query.

metrics.description: Evaluation metrics captured for this approach/query.

BO-1.description: Evaluate AI capabilities that combine structured and unstructured data.

BO-2.description: Find a scalable lower-cost solution for unstructured or hybrid structured/unstructured retrieval workloads.

BO-3.description: Reduce storage and indexing cost for embeddings/search workloads compared with the current Elastic-based approach.

BO-4.description: Achieve very low-latency retrieval over large document sets for downstream agent use.

BO-5.description: Validate vendor claims with real demos, benchmarks, comparisons, and hands-on proof before making decisions.

FR-1.description: Support document search over unstructured content provided by customers, including PDFs and other uploaded document types.

FR-2.description: Support use cases that combine structured and unstructured data in retrieval workflows.

FR-3.description: Support agent memory/context retrieval from conversation-derived documents.

FR-4.description: Support retrieval and re-ranking so relevant results can be surfaced to agents.

FR-5.description: Handle large-scale vector retrieval across approximately one million documents in a single index.

FR-6.description: Support a POV/demo workflow where users can upload documents during the session and ask questions against them.

FR-7.description: Demonstrate multiple chunking strategies for document processing, including fixed-length, recursive, semantic, and contextual chunking.

FR-8.description: Support isolated per-customer SaaS deployments in addition to some multi-tenant services.

FR-9.description: Support tagging or access association at the document level for context records tied to users and tenants.

AI-1.description: Provide vector search capabilities for unstructured document retrieval.

AI-2.description: Enable embeddings generation and retrieval workflows for customer documents.

AI-3.description: Support PDF/document ingestion where users may upload unpredictable document types and still expect useful retrieval outcomes.

AI-4.description: Support retrieval accuracy benchmarking using customer-provided questions/ground truth.

AI-5.description: Evaluate retrieval quality using top-k based measures up to top 20.

AI-6.description: Compare retrieval precision, recall, and latency during the evaluation.

AI-7.description: Potentially support multimodal retrieval in the future, but it is not part of the requested benchmark flow for the next demo.

AI-8.description: Support agent conversation/session data as a backend database use case.

SC-1.description: Show that document search works well on customer-like documents uploaded during the demo.

SC-2.description: Demonstrate retrieval at the right latency for the document-search use case.

SC-3.description: Provide side-by-side comparison against a baseline or current system to determine whether there is significant difference.

SC-4.description: Demonstrate raw retrieval accuracy and speed using the same documents across systems.

SC-5.description: Evaluate precision, recall, and latency metrics in the demo/POV.

SC-6.description: Assess top-k retrieval quality at top 1, 5, 10, and 20.

SC-7.description: Validate that MongoDB/Voyage offers better results than the customer’s current or simple baseline approach rather than merely matching it.

SC-8.description: Potential future success criterion: support around 400-500 concurrent requests, though this is not the immediate focus of the POV.

INT-1.description: Integrate with or replace parts of the current Elastic/Elastic Cloud based search and embeddings workflow.

INT-2.description: Coexist with Postgres, which is currently used as the application database and for some metadata.

INT-3.description: Coexist with S3, which currently stores raw documents.

INT-4.description: Fit into environments that already use OpenSearch for some customer deployments/use cases.

INT-5.description: Work within a multi-cloud environment across AWS, GCP, and/or other clouds.

INT-6.description: Potentially align with Vertex AI-based session management already in use for agents.

INT-7.description: Support content originating from connectors such as Slack, Confluence, Jira, Google Sheets, CSVs, and PDFs.
